scope: Second technical and ergonomic audit of the shared header, account menu, command palette, mobile workspace tabs, footer grid and retired account-profile boundary.
findings: Tablet widths from 768px through 1023px previously exposed both the desktop header links and the fixed mobile bottom bar; the bottom bar and main-content reservation now use the same md breakpoint.
The footer retained a fourth navigation track after the account column was removed; the desktop grid now matches its three visible navigation columns.
The mobile bottom tab now says Library, matching the /images/library destination and the user's saved-work mental model.
Header and drawer controls meet the 44px touch-target floor; the account menu supports menu semantics, Arrow/Home/End traversal, Escape dismissal and focus return.

The command palette is a labelled modal with focus containment and restoration, a valid combobox/listbox relationship, active-option metadata, backdrop dismissal, an authored no-match state and a 44px close target.

validation.production_build: npm run build passed; Next generated 163 pages and the route manifests contain no /settings route.
validation.retired_surface_scan: Compiled HTML/JS/JSON contains no /settings?tab=profile or app/settings/page references; /teams/settings is a separate existing team route.
validation.lint: npm run lint passed with zero errors and eight pre-existing warnings outside this navigation scope.
validation.ux_detector: The deterministic Impeccable detector returned no findings for the audited navigation, command, layout and footer files.
validation.security_navigation: npm run test:image:security passed 55/55; node --import tsx --test scripts/test-url-navigation.ts passed 5/5.
validation.documentation_tests: npm run test:docs passed 17/17; npm run docs:sync completed successfully. docs:impact maps all product source edits and leaves only this retained audit plus generated review metadata outside source ownership.

limits: No live deployment or hosted browser acceptance is implied.
The account-profile data/API schema remains untouched; only the unsupported settings navigation surface stays retired.
